findings.detail: UK Student visa application fee was £524 and is £558. The Home Office fee table changed on 8 April 2026, so this had been wrong on the live site for roughly six months. Verified on gov.uk/student-visa, which states £558 to apply from outside the UK. Corrected in src/modules/cost/data.ts.

Every exchange rate was set in August 2026 and understated the rupee cost of studying abroad by 10 to 19 percent. Against Nepal Rastra Bank's published selling rates for 1 October 2026: USD 138 to 153.64, EUR 152 to 174.56, GBP 178 to 204.07, AUD 90 to 107.12, CAD 98 to 108.35. Five of six corrected. This fed every NPR figure on the calculator and on all six /study/ pages with a cost table.

The NZD rate of 82 could not be verified and was NOT changed. Nepal Rastra Bank publishes no NZD rate at all; its list runs INR, USD, EUR, GBP, CHF, AUD, CAD, SGD, JPY, CNY, SAR, QAR, THB, AED, MYR, KRW, SEK, DKK, HKD, KWD, BHD and OMR. Because the other five rates were corrected and this one could not be, New Zealand now renders cheaper than it is relative to the other destinations. Needs a sourcing decision.

The page said Migri normally wants a bank statement covering the preceding three months. Migri's income requirement page says six months. A student who prepares three months of statements fails on the document, not on the money. Corrected. The EUR 9,600 and EUR 800 figures themselves are confirmed correct, as is the own-account rule.

The figures are correct (EUR 10,000 for a one year course, EUR 833 a month, EUR 6,665 for eight months) but the source line credited them to 'courses beginning after 1 July 2023'. The Irish Immigration Service now dates the monthly structure to 30 June 2025. Citation updated; no figure changed.

All four /software/ pages declared offers.price '0' in SoftwareApplication JSON-LD, stating OfficeYak is free. The pages' own FAQ answers 'is there a free version?' with 'not permanently', the cheapest consultancy plan is NPR 4,999 a month, and the homepage declares 4,999, 12,999 and 29,999. The same product was priced two ways on one site. Now declares the real Starter price from src/lib/plans.ts. Affects all four software pages.

The sources list cited https://mols.gov.np, which has no DNS record. The ministry was reorganised into the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment in May 2026 and its site is www.moless.gov.np, which loads and carries the Labour Act 2074 and the Contribution-based Social Security Act 2074. Link and label corrected.

https://www.ocr.gov.np (Office of the Company Registrar) returned HTTP 503 on every attempt, by curl and by fetch tool. The domain is correct and this looks like their outage, so the link was left alone. Worth a recheck next run; if it is still 503 the guide needs a line telling readers the registrar's site is down rather than sending them to a dead page.

The Australian visa application charge of AUD 2,000 could not be checked. Every Home Affairs fees URL returned HTTP 403 to automated requests, on immi.homeaffairs.gov.au and homeaffairs.gov.au alike, and the subclass 500 page that did fetch does not carry the charge. No substitute source was used and the figure was not changed. Australia's funds figure of AUD 29,710 WAS verified from that page and is correct.

The NOC fee of NPR 2,000, which the page dates 'as at August 2026', could not be verified. moest.gov.np links to the NOC portal but publishes no fee schedule, and noc.moest.gov.np exposes nothing a fetch can read without logging in. Not changed and not re-dated. The page also quotes NPR 8,000 and NPR 15,000 as examples of consultancy mark-up, which are illustrative rather than sourced and read correctly as such.

The guide states the usual GIC amount is CAD 20,635 and builds a whole section on it being below the CAD 23,448 requirement. The CAD 23,448 and CAD 22,895 figures are confirmed correct from IRCC. The GIC amount is not a government figure: IRCC publishes no GIC amount now that SDS is discontinued, banks set it. House style says a figure that cannot be sourced from an official government page should not be on the page. Left unchanged pending a decision, because the argument it supports is sound even if the number needs a different treatment.

The scholarship NPR values in src/modules/finder/scholarships.ts were computed from the old exchange rates and are now inconsistent with the corrected ones. Chevening's '£10,000' is valued at NPR 1,780,000, which is exactly 10,000 times the old GBP rate of 178; at 204.07 it is about 2,040,700. Destination Australia's 'AUD 15,000' at NPR 1,350,000 is 15,000 times the old AUD 90. Not changed: src/modules/finder is outside what this routine may edit without asking, and several of the eleven ranges mix tuition with living costs so they cannot all be recomputed mechanically.

12 of 52 pages carry no JSON-LD at all: the three hub pages /software, /blog and /tools, and all nine tool pages (/tools/eligibility, /tools/cost, /tools/loan, /tools/checklist, /tools/document-checklist, /tools/universities, /tools/scholarships, /tools/compare, /tools/cv-maker). The tools are the top of the funnel per the brief and are the pages most likely to earn a rich result. Not added: nine new schema blocks is new work rather than re-verification.

Renders only about 947 characters of server-side text with JavaScript off, against 2,858 on /tools/compare, 3,296 on /tools/cost and 6,706 on the homepage. The tool itself works without JS; there is simply almost no prose for a crawler to read. Lowest-content page on the site.

suggestions.title: Decide where the NZD exchange rate comes from
suggestions.detail: Nepal Rastra Bank publishes no NZD rate, so there is no official Nepali source for it. The other five rates are now NRB's 1 October selling rates and NZD is still August's 82. Options: accept a licensed Nepali commercial bank's published NZD rate and say on the page that it comes from a bank rather than NRB; or derive it from NRB's USD rate and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's published NZD/USD, labelled as derived from two official sources; or drop the NPR conversion on /study/new-zealand and show NZD only. A run should not pick between these on its own.
suggestions.why: Until it is decided, New Zealand looks roughly a tenth cheaper than the others on the comparison tool, which is an artefact of our sourcing rather than a fact about New Zealand, and the compare tool ranks destinations by rupee cost.
suggestions.needsYou: Pick one of the three sourcing options. This is the only figure on the site that is knowingly unverified.

suggestions.title: Review the structured-data price change on the four software pages
suggestions.detail: The offer now declares NPR 4,999 a month from src/lib/plans.ts instead of 0. The reasoning is in a comment at src/app/software/[slug]/page.tsx: the pages' own FAQ says there is no permanent free version, and the homepage already declared the three real prices, so a 0 had one product priced two ways. The consequence is that a Google rich result may now show a price where it previously showed free. Reverting is a one-line change if you would rather it said free on the strength of the student free tier and the 30 day trial.
suggestions.why: It changes what a buyer sees in search results before they reach the site, so it is a commercial call rather than a technical one, even though the contradiction it fixes was real.
suggestions.needsYou: Confirm you want the real price declared, or tell the routine to revert it.

suggestions.title: Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY so the AI tool pages can be written
suggestions.detail: Three queued pages (ai ielts preparation, ai pte preparation, ai mock interview and its variant) are blocked on one credential. The tools exist in the product and answer with sample text until OFFICEYAK_AI_PROVIDER is set to anthropic-api with a key behind it. Blocked for a third consecutive run.
suggestions.why: The student queue notes these carry more search volume than anything else left in it, and the student side is the top of the funnel for the whole business.
suggestions.needsYou: Add the key to the environment. Blocked since at least 26 September.

suggestions.title: Hamro CRM cannot be reached from the routine's environment
suggestions.detail: hamrocrm.com fails DNS resolution (EAI_AGAIN) from both curl and the fetch tool, and an earlier attempt failed at the proxy with CONNECT tunnel failed, response 502. Search results confirm the site is alive and actively publishing, so this is an environment problem. Their section in competitors.md is therefore built from search results rather than from their pages.
suggestions.why: The brief names Hamro CRM as the one competitor to watch, and it is the one competitor this routine currently cannot see.
suggestions.needsYou: Needs someone to check whether the network policy or the proxy resolver is blocking this host.

suggestions.title: Decide how to treat the CAD 20,635 GIC figure
suggestions.detail: IRCC no longer publishes a GIC amount, because the Student Direct Stream it belonged to is discontinued; banks set it. House style says a figure with no official government page behind it should not be on the page, but the Canada guide's GIC section is built on this one and the point it makes, that a GIC alone does not cover the CAD 23,448 requirement, is correct and useful.
suggestions.why: It is the only figure on the site that is both load-bearing for a reader's planning and not sourceable from a government page.
suggestions.needsYou: Either attribute it to the banks explicitly, or rewrite the section to make the point without a specific GIC number.

suggestions.title: Add structured data to the nine tool pages and three hub pages
suggestions.detail: 12 of 52 pages have no JSON-LD. The tools are the top of the funnel and are the pages most likely to win a rich result. Not done this run because the monthly playbook publishes nothing new and nine new schema blocks is new work.
suggestions.why: Mechanical, low risk, and the pages it would help are the ones the brief says must not be treated as a side project.

suggestions.title: Give /tools/eligibility some prose
suggestions.detail: It renders about 947 characters of server-side text, the thinnest page on the site, against 3,296 on /tools/cost. The tool works fine without JavaScript; there is just nothing for a crawler to read.
suggestions.why: It is a page with real search intent behind it and almost no content to rank.

suggestions.title: Correct the competitor table in the brief: Pace CRM is not thin
suggestions.detail: docs/routines/officeyak.md lists Pace CRM (thepaceinfosys.com) as thin and barely publishing. Their sitemap holds 98 URLs of which 72 are blog posts, and they hold /products/crm/consultancy-crm-software titled 'Best CRM for Education Consultancy in Nepal', a direct hit on our Tier 1 term.
suggestions.why: The daily routine reads that table to decide which competitors are worth checking, so a wrong entry means a real competitor goes unwatched.

suggestions.title: Recompute the scholarship NPR ranges, or decide not to
suggestions.detail: The eleven ranges in src/modules/finder/scholarships.ts were derived from the August exchange rates and are now 10 to 19 percent low. Some are pure arithmetic on a stated foreign-currency award (Chevening's £10,000 at NPR 1,780,000 is 10,000 x 178) and some blend tuition with living costs, so they cannot all be recomputed mechanically. src/modules/finder is also outside what this routine may edit without asking.
suggestions.why: A student comparing a scholarship's rupee value against a cost calculator that now uses current rates is comparing two different exchange rates on the same site.
suggestions.needsYou: Confirm whether the routine may edit src/modules/finder, and whether the blended ranges should be rebuilt or left as broad estimates.

summary:
Five of six exchange rates were understating rupee costs by 10 to 19 percent and are now Nepal Rastra Bank's 1 October selling rates. The UK visa fee had been £524 since the Home Office raised it to £558 in April.
Every published funds requirement checked out correct: UK, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Ireland, Finland and the US position on the I-20. Finland's statement period was wrong at three months and is six.
The four software pages declared the product free in structured data while their own FAQ says there is no permanent free version. Fixed to the real Starter price; revert it if you would rather it said free.
Three figures could not be verified and were flagged rather than kept quietly: the NZD rate, which NRB does not publish at all, the Australian visa charge, and the NOC fee. Nothing was removed or merged, because four days of Search Console data cannot justify deleting a page.
